Reproducing Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) from dandiset 001260¶

Paper. Le Merre P, Heining K, Slashcheva M, Jung F, Moysiadou E, Guyon N, Yahya R, Park H, Wernstal F, Carlén M. A prefrontal cortex map based on single-neuron activity. Nature Neuroscience (2026). doi:10.1038/s41593-025-02190-z. The claims file (claims/001260/10.1038-s41593-025-02190-z.yaml) was written from the version of record (publisher HTML: main text, legends, Methods and Extended Data legends); the Supplementary Information was not available to it.

Dandiset. DANDI:001260, version 0.250911.0744. The paper cites no version. This is the only published version, and the draft has the same 74 assets and size, so it is pinned.

Other data. The paper deposits its dataset KI in two dandisets, 000473 and 001260 (Data availability). Dandiset 000473 (version 0.230417.1502, the only published one; its metadata names another paper) holds 25 more recordings; it is read for the unit counts of dataset-ki-counts and fig1h-waveform-classes, the dataROI count of fig4b, and as a variant of fig4e; every other analysis runs on 001260. From the paper's Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.14205018 this attempt reads the Harris et al. hierarchy table (hierarchy_summary_CreConf.xlsx), the per-unit metrics files (metrics_files.zip, for each unit's flatmap position and the paper's quality flags), the flatmap polygons including the paper's 42 dataROIs (flatmaps.zip), the Gao et al. ROI hierarchy table (ROI_Gao_hierarchy_index.csv), and, for variants only, the paper's own sleep-like detection (quiet_active_detection.zip) and its trained SOMs (SOMs.zip).

Methods. The helper module pfcki.py says where every parameter comes from. Sleep-like periods are detected per recording session from the pooled cortical units of its probes, and not at all in sessions with too few cortical units for the detector (an assumption, examined in extfig1-epoch-counts). The unit counts follow the Methods' unit quality control (6 spikes in 12 spontaneous epochs); every other analysis keeps units with at least 12 active spontaneous epochs of at least 6 spikes. Units are not filtered by a quality label, as the files carry none.

Claims. Tested here: the claims on dataset KI's spontaneous activity (Figs. 1 and 2, Extended Data Figs. 1, 3 and 5), the Harris hierarchy correlations (Fig. 3a,c, Supplementary Table 5) with the Harris table, the PFC flatmap claims (Fig. 4) through the Zenodo flatmap positions after a link claim, and the tone-response claims on dataset KI (Fig. 5b to 5f, the dataset part of 5i, 5j, Extended Data Fig. 9e). Blocked: every claim on dataset IBL (Figs. 2i, 3b, 5g, 5h, 5k), not attempted, and methods-settings-no-difference, whose test the paper does not name. Several enrichment and hierarchy claims are blocked by the claims file's own rule because their outcome depends on which retrained cluster takes which category number (G2). The table of outcomes is in the summary.

import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import pfcki as P

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

t_start = time.time()
assets = P.list_assets()
recs = P.classify_epochs(P.load_all(assets))
U = P.unit_table(recs)
print(f"dandiset {P.DANDISET} version {P.VERSION}: {len(assets)} assets, {len(recs)} files read, "
      f"{len(U)} units, in {time.time() - t_start:.0f} s")
assets473 = P.list_assets(P.OTHER_DANDISET, P.OTHER_VERSION)
recs473 = P.classify_epochs(P.load_all(assets473))
U473 = P.unit_table(recs473)
print(f"dandiset {P.OTHER_DANDISET} version {P.OTHER_VERSION}: {len(recs473)} files, {len(U473)} units, "
      f"total {time.time() - t_start:.0f} s")
# outside inputs from the paper's Zenodo record: per-unit metrics files and its own sleep-like detection
Z = P.paper_unit_table()
PQ = P.paper_quiet()
print(f"Zenodo: {Z.session.nunique()} recordings in the metrics files, {len(PQ)} sleep-like detection files")

The archive counts 43 subjects, as the subject ids of two mice recorded on two days carry the suffixes -1 and -2 (518804 and 560171); without the suffixes the files hold 41 mice, which with the 25 mice of 000473 make the paper's 66. The setting read from each file's description agrees with the setting the paper's code assigns to the same recording (config/datatables/allrecs_allprobes.xlsx) for every file: Aversion 6, Detection 15, Context 14, working memory ("Attention" in the code) 15, Opto 4, Passive 20. Five auditory-cortex probes are described as Neuronexus recordings; the paper pools them as probes of dataset KI.

def rng_str(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    return f"{np.nanmin(x):.3g} to {np.nanmax(x):.3g} (median {np.nanmedian(x):.3g})"

print("Peak_to_Trough (ms):", rng_str(U.Peak_to_Trough if "Peak_to_Trough" in U else U.ptt))
print("quality column 0, 'ISI violation':", rng_str(U.q_isi), "| fraction < 0.1:", round((U.q_isi < 0.1).mean(), 3))
print("quality column 1, 'false positive rate':", rng_str(U.q_fp), "| fraction < 0.1:", round((U.q_fp < 0.1).mean(), 3))
print("spikes per unit:", rng_str(U.n_spikes))
print("unit locations: ", U.location.nunique(), "labels;", (U.layer != "NA").mean().round(3), "of units have a layer")
print("units per parent region:"); print(U.parent.value_counts().to_string())
print("\nAll units in both dandisets:", len(U), "+", len(U473), "=", len(U) + len(U473),
      "| paper: 34,642 sorted, 29,782 after excluding 24 recordings, 24,248 after quality control")

The two dandisets hold 29,782 units together, exactly the paper's count after it excluded 24 recordings and before its unit quality control, so the files hold every sorted unit of the 99 recordings and no label says which units passed. The units table has a two-column quality (ISI violation, false positive rate). The first column runs to hundreds, so it is not the ISI violation ratio below 0.1 of the Methods in the same units; fewer than half of the units are below 0.1 on it. Its meaning is not described. The peak-to-trough durations are in ms, as stated, and agree with the paper's Zenodo metrics files (shown in the link claim).

# Column descriptions of the trials and electrodes tables, one file per setting
first = {}
for r in recs:
    first.setdefault(r["setting"], r)
for sname, r in first.items():
    f = P.open_asset(r["asset_id"])
    tr = f["intervals/trials"]
    desc = {k: P.dec(tr[k].attrs.get("description", "")) for k in tr.keys() if k != "id"}
    sound = tr["sound"][:] if "sound" in tr else None
    el = f["general/extracellular_ephys/electrodes"]
    eld = sorted({P.dec(el[k].attrs.get("description", "")) for k in el.keys() if k != "id"})
    f.close()
    print(f"{sname} ({r['session']}): trials {len(r['onsets'])} onsets; trial columns: {desc}")
    if sound is not None:
        print(f"   'sound' True in {int(np.sum(sound))} of {len(sound)} trials; 10-kHz tones in the file: "
              f"{0 if r['tones'] is None else len(r['tones'])}")
    print(f"   electrode column descriptions: {eld}")

In the Detection and Context files the trials columns lick and valve are described as "sound amplitude"; in the Detection file the Block column is described as the trial type (miss, hit, correct rejection, false alarm), not a block. In the Context file sound is False for all 524 trials though the file holds 524 10-kHz tones. The electrode columns (including location, AP, DV, ML) are all described as "my description". The values were read as their names say; location agrees with the paper's Zenodo files for 98.6% of units (zenodo-unit-link). Because the Detection Block column alternates, those recordings are cut into blocks of 50 onsets (fig2e-category-stability).

Epoch length is 3 s for every epoch: True
Onsets per file: 163 to 535 (median 378) | active: 29 to 375 (median 215)
Intervals between successive onsets outside the working-memory setting (s): [ 4.08  5.21  8.51 16.32 30.64] (Methods: tones at random intervals of 5 to 10 s)

Licking is marked in 44 files (LickOnset and LickOffset series), saturation of the spike band in most. Sleep-like periods are detected per recording session from the cortical units of all its probes pooled (Methods: "detected per recording session ... across all cortical spikes"). Where the detector marks 1% of the time or more in a Poisson population with the session's pooled rate (column "null %"), the session has too few cortical units for it and no sleep-like period is marked; nor for the four hippocampal probes the code's table marks "ignore". This skip rule is this attempt's own, not the paper's: the Methods say detection "was only performed for the dataset KI, as sessions of this dataset consistently featured a sufficient number of cortical units to detect collective off periods", and skip no session. It was chosen because the paper's own detection files mark some recordings off_used = no; it is an assumption, examined in extfig1-epoch-counts. Outside the working-memory setting the intervals between onsets have a median of 8.5 s (5th to 95th percentile 5.2 to 16.3 s), close to the Methods' 5 to 10 s; 1% are below 4.1 s. In the working-memory setting the code's onsets are trial starts. The 3-s epochs are 3 s long.

Clock check. The spike times and the stimulus onsets must share a clock: below, the population rate of PFC units in 25-ms bins around the 10-kHz tone onsets of each file, against the same with the onsets shifted by 1.5 s (a time with no tone). A response locked to the true onsets, and not to the shifted ones, shows the clocks agree.

In [6]:
def tone_contrast(r, shift):
    """Mean rate of all units 0 to 100 ms after the onsets minus 100 to 0 ms before, in Hz per unit."""
    if r["tones"] is None:
        return np.nan
    f = P.open_asset(r["asset_id"])
    st = f["units/spike_times"][:]
    f.close()
    t = r["tones"] + shift
    st.sort()
    post = np.searchsorted(st, t + 0.1) - np.searchsorted(st, t)
    pre = np.searchsorted(st, t) - np.searchsorted(st, t - 0.1)
    return (post.sum() - pre.sum()) / len(t) / 0.1 / len(r["units"])

sample = [r for r in recs if r["tones"] is not None][::6]
cc = pd.DataFrame([{"session": r["session"], "true onsets": tone_contrast(r, 0.0),
                    "shifted 1.5 s": tone_contrast(r, 1.5)} for r in sample])
print("Post minus pre rate (Hz per unit) around 10-kHz tone onsets, every sixth file with tones:")
print(cc.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("files with a larger change at the true onsets than at the shifted ones:",
      int((cc["true onsets"].abs() > cc["shifted 1.5 s"].abs()).sum()), "of", len(cc))

In every sampled file the rate change at the true onsets is larger than at onsets shifted by 1.5 s (an increase in nine, a decrease in one somatosensory recording), so spikes and onsets share a clock there. The other files with tones are consistent with it: their units enter the tone categories of fig5b, whose responses peak tens of ms after the onsets.

dataset-ki-counts¶

Dataset KI holds 24,248 single units from 99 Neuropixels recordings in awake head-fixed mice, 52% of them in the PFC and 48% in other brain regions.

Readings of the unit selection (claims file, G3): (a) the dataset's own quality metrics under the Methods criteria, read as column 0 (ISI violation) below 0.1 or column 1 (false positive rate) below 0.1; (b) all units. Each also needs the Methods' epoch rule. The count of 24,248 is the one of the Methods' Unit quality control, which requires "a sufficient number of ISIs (≥4) in at least 12 separate 3-s epochs" and does not restrict them to active epochs; the Methods' Spontaneous firing metrics read "at least six spikes (corresponding to at least four ISIs)". The main rule here takes both passages: at least 6 spikes in at least 12 spontaneous epochs, active or sleep-like (epochs with licking or saturation excluded). At least 5 spikes, and only active epochs (the claims header's rule for the metrics, which the analyses of the later claims keep), are shown as variants, as is the paper's own quality flag from Zenodo.

In [7]:
def n_valid_with(recs_, min_spikes, states):
    out = []
    for r in recs_:
        m = np.isin(r["state"], states)
        out.append((r["cnt"][:, m] >= min_spikes).sum(1))
    return np.concatenate(out)

SPONT = ["active", "near_sleep", "sleep"]
for D, rr in [(U, recs), (U473, recs473)]:
    D["n_qc"] = n_valid_with(rr, 6, SPONT)        # main: Unit quality control passage, 6 spikes = "4 ISIs"
    D["n_qc5"] = n_valid_with(rr, 5, SPONT)
    D["n_act5"] = n_valid_with(rr, 5, ["active"])
UK = pd.concat([U, U473], ignore_index=True)
UK = UK.merge(Z[["session", "unit_id", "z_quality", "z_wquality"]], on=["session", "unit_id"], how="left")
UK["z_pass"] = (UK.z_quality == 1) & (UK.z_wquality == 1)
rec_counts = {"001260": len(recs), "001260 + 000473": len(recs) + len(recs473)}

def count_table(D, label, col):
    rows = []
    for g3, m in [("(a) ISI violation < 0.1", D.q_isi < 0.1), ("(a) false positive rate < 0.1", D.q_fp < 0.1),
                  ("(b) all units", np.ones(len(D), bool))]:
        k = D[m & (D[col] >= P.MIN_EPOCHS)]
        rows.append({"data": label, "reading": g3, "units": len(k), "PFC units": int(k.is_pfc.sum()),
                     "PFC %": round(100 * k.is_pfc.mean(), 1)})
    return rows

print("Main rule (>= 6 spikes in >= 12 spontaneous epochs, active or sleep-like):")
print(pd.DataFrame(count_table(U, "001260", "n_qc") + count_table(UK, "001260 + 000473", "n_qc")).to_string(index=False))
print("recordings (probes):", rec_counts, "| expected 24,248 ± 2,425 units, 52 ± 5.2 % PFC, 99 recordings, 12,674 ± 1,267 PFC units")

var = []
for lab, D in [("001260", U), ("001260 + 000473", UK)]:
    for col, ms, sl in [("n_qc", 6, "all spontaneous"), ("n_qc5", 5, "all spontaneous"),
                        ("n_act5", 5, "active"), ("n_valid", 6, "active")]:
        k = D[D[col] >= P.MIN_EPOCHS]
        var.append({"data": lab, "min spikes": ms, "epochs": sl, "units": len(k),
                    "PFC %": round(100 * k.is_pfc.mean(), 1), "PFC units": int(k.is_pfc.sum())})

            "units": len(k), "PFC %": round(100 * k.is_pfc.mean(), 1), "PFC units": int(k.is_pfc.sum())})

Result: reproduced. On 001260 + 000473 the recordings are the paper's 99, and under the main rule (reading b, at least 6 spikes in 12 spontaneous epochs) there are 24,898 units (24,248 ± 2,425), 52.4% in the PFC (52 ± 5.2) and 13,040 PFC units (12,674 ± 1,267). Every other epoch rule under reading (b) also falls within tolerance: 25,929, 23,168 and 22,091 units, 52.3%, 51.9% and 52.1% PFC, 13,559, 12,026 and 11,509 PFC units; with the paper's own quality flags from Zenodo 24,270 units remain. Reading (a) of the files' undescribed quality columns gives far fewer (6,561 or 16,545). 001260 alone holds 74 recordings and 17,205 such units, 47.3% in the PFC.

fig1h-waveform-classes¶

Peak-to-trough durations are bimodal, splitting units into 19,186 ww units (81.1%) and 4,200 nw units (17.7%), with 862 intermediate units left unclassified.

def wf_row(lab, rule, k):
    n = k.utype.value_counts()
    tot, cls = len(k), n.get("ww", 0) + n.get("nw", 0)
    return {"data": lab, "selection": rule, "ww": n.get("ww", 0), "nw": n.get("nw", 0), "unclassified": n.get("na", 0),
            "ww % of all": round(100 * n.get("ww", 0) / tot, 1), "nw % of all": round(100 * n.get("nw", 0) / tot, 1),
            "ww % of ww+nw": round(100 * n.get("ww", 0) / cls, 1), "nw % of ww+nw": round(100 * n.get("nw", 0) / cls, 1)}

wf = []
for lab, D in [("001260", U), ("001260 + 000473", UK)]:
    for rule, col in [("main: >= 6 spikes, 12 spontaneous epochs", "n_qc"), (">= 5 spikes, 12 spontaneous epochs", "n_qc5"),
                      (">= 6 spikes, 12 active epochs", "n_valid")]:
        for g3, m in [("(b) all units", np.ones(len(D), bool)), ("(a) false positive rate < 0.1", D.q_fp < 0.1)]:
            wf.append(wf_row(lab, f"{rule}, {g3}", D[m & (D[col] >= P.MIN_EPOCHS)]))
        if lab != "001260":
            wf.append(wf_row(lab, f"{rule}, Zenodo quality flags", D[D.z_pass & (D[col] >= P.MIN_EPOCHS)]))
print(pd.DataFrame(wf).to_string(index=False))

Result: reproduced (under the main rule, an assumption). On 001260 + 000473 with at least 6 spikes in 12 spontaneous epochs, there are 19,731 ww units (19,186 ± 1,919), 4,247 nw (4,200 ± 420) and 920 unclassified (862 ± 86); ww are 79.2% and nw 17.1% of all units (82.3% and 17.7% of ww plus nw), within 81.1 ± 8.1 and 17.7 ± 1.8. The readings of the epoch rule differ in one count each: with at least 5 spikes the unclassified units are 951, just above 948; with active epochs only, the ww units are 17,239, just below 17,267. With the paper's Zenodo quality flags all three counts fall within tolerance (19,182, 4,181, 907). The histogram has a mode at 0.26 ms (475 units) and one at 0.64 ms (1,340) with a minimum at 0.36 ms (298).

fig1i-nw-higher-metrics¶

Narrow-waveform units have significantly higher firing rates, burstiness and memory than wide-waveform units.

Mixed model Metric ~ 1 + Unittype + (1|Mouse) per metric (Methods, equation 6), fitted with statsmodels (REML). The paper's Kenward-Roger F test is not available there; the Wald test of the unit-type coefficient is used (with thousands of units and 40 mice the degrees of freedom are large either way). With one comparison per metric Tukey's correction changes nothing.

extfig1d-sleep-like-differ¶

Firing metrics in sleep-like epochs differ from those in active spontaneous epochs, which is why sleep-like epochs are excluded.

ww units with at least 12 active epochs (active sample) and ww units with at least 12 sleep-like epochs of at least 6 spikes (sleep-like sample), Metric ~ 1 + EpochType + (1|Mouse) (Methods, equation 7). Sleep-like periods from the Methods' detector per session (main); the same detector per probe, the code's detector, the main detector without sleep-like periods in the sessions the paper's own detection files mark as not using it (off_used = no), and the paper's own sleep-like periods (Zenodo quiet_active_detection.zip, an outside input) are variants.

In [10]:
def epoch_type_models(Ux):
    ww_ = Ux[Ux.utype == "ww"]
    a = ww_[ww_.n_valid >= P.MIN_EPOCHS][["subject", "log10FR", "B", "M"]].assign(epoch="active")
    s = ww_[ww_.n_valid_sleep >= P.MIN_EPOCHS][["subject", "log10FR_sleep", "B_sleep", "M_sleep"]]
    s = s.rename(columns=lambda c: c.replace("_sleep", "")).assign(epoch="sleep")
    L = pd.concat([a, s]).dropna()
    rows = []
    for m in ["log10FR", "B", "M"]:
        f, _ = P.mixed(L, f"{m} ~ C(epoch)")
        rows.append({"metric": m, "sleep - active": f.params.iloc[1], "p": f.pvalues.iloc[1],
                     "median active": a[m].median(), "median sleep": s[m].median()})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), len(a), len(s)

res, na_, ns_ = epoch_type_models(U)
print(f"Methods detector: {na_} ww units with >= 12 active epochs, {ns_} with >= 12 sleep-like epochs "
      "(paper, all of dataset KI: 19,186 and 11,599)")
print(res.to_string(index=False))
def with_sleep(recs_, fn):
    """copies of the records with the sleep-like periods fn(r) and the epoch states recomputed"""
    out = []
    for r in recs_:
        r2 = dict(r)
        r2["sleep"] = fn(r)
        ep = r2["epochs"]
        bad = P.overlaps(ep, r2["lick"]) | P.overlaps(ep, r2["sat"])
        sl = r2["sleep"]
        if sl is None or len(sl) == 0:
            s_, near = np.zeros(len(ep), bool), np.zeros(len(ep), bool)
        else:
            s_, near = P.overlaps(ep, sl), P.overlaps(ep, sl, pad=1.0)
        r2["state"] = np.where(bad, "excluded", np.where(s_, "sleep", np.where(near, "near_sleep", "active")))
        out.append(r2)
    return out

def paper_flag(r):
    """'yes' when a probe of the session has the paper's off_used = yes, 'no' when its files all say no"""
    day = r["session"].rsplit("-", 1)[0]
    fl = [q["used"] for k, q in PQ.items() if k.rsplit("-", 1)[0] == day]
    return "yes" if "yes" in fl else ("no" if fl else "no file")

def paper_periods(r):
    """the paper's own sleep-like periods: the probe's file, else another probe's of the session"""
    day = r["session"].rsplit("-", 1)[0]
    k = r["session"] if r["session"] in PQ else next((k for k in PQ if k.rsplit("-", 1)[0] == day), None)
    return None if k is None else PQ[k]["quiet"]

VAR = {}
for det in ["methods", "code"]:
    rr_ = P.classify_epochs([dict(r) for r in recs], detector=det)
    VAR[det] = (rr_, P.unit_table(rr_))
    res_v, na_v, ns_v = epoch_type_models(VAR[det][1])
    print(f"\nVariant, {'the Methods detector per probe (round 1)' if det == 'methods' else 'the code detector per probe'}: "
          f"{na_v} and {ns_v} units")
    print(res_v.to_string(index=False))
for det, fn in [("flags", lambda r: None if paper_flag(r) == "no" else r["sleep"]), ("paper", paper_periods)]:
    rr_ = with_sleep(recs, fn)
    VAR[det] = (rr_, P.unit_table(rr_))
    res_v, na_v, ns_v = epoch_type_models(VAR[det][1])
    print(f"\nVariant, {'the main detector with none where the paper says off_used = no' if det == 'flags' else 'the paper own sleep-like periods (Zenodo)'}: "
          f"{na_v} and {ns_v} units")
    print(res_v.to_string(index=False))

With sleep-like periods detected per session, sleep-like epochs differ from active ones in B (+0.031, p = 5.3e-63) and M (-0.011, p = 2.3e-12) but not in log10FR (+0.008, p = 0.14), from 12,112 active and 8,405 sleep-like samples: two of three metrics. With the detector per probe, the code's detector, or the paper's own sleep-like periods from Zenodo all three metrics differ (log10FR p = 4.4e-06, 0.0012 and 0.0027), the log10FR difference changing sign between them (-0.024, +0.018, +0.019); B and M differ in the same direction under every detector.

extfig1-epoch-counts¶

Sleep-like episodes occupy a median 6% (IQR 0 to 18%) of recording time; sessions hold a median 227 (IQR 172 to 284) spontaneous active epochs and 19 (IQR 1 to 84) sleep-like epochs.

Readings of "recording session": one probe recording (file), or one session of up to three probes (subject and date; time fraction and epochs from the session's first probe, as all probes of a session share onsets). The recording time is from the first to the last spike. Detectors: the Methods detector per session (main), per probe (variant, round 1's main), the code's detector (variant); and two variants that use the paper's own detection on Zenodo (quiet_active_detection.zip, an outside input): the main detector, but no sleep-like period in the sessions whose probes the paper's files mark as not using off-period detection (off_used = no), and the paper's own sleep-like periods.

The second cell below prints the per-probe check of the detector asked for in review: the number of cortical units and their mean rate, the share of time marked sleep-like by each detector, the share it marks in a Poisson population with the same pooled rate and no off periods (null), the median EMG RMS (1-s windows, processing/ecephys/EMG) in sleep-like time over that in the rest of the recording, and the paper's own flag and share.

def epoch_table(recs_):
    rows = []
    for r in recs_:
        rows.append({"session": r["session"], "day": r["session"].split("-")[0],
                     "sleep %": 100 * P.sleep_fraction(r["sleep"], r["t0"], r["t1"]),
                     "active epochs": int((r["state"] == "active").sum()), "sleep-like epochs": int((r["state"] == "sleep").sum())})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def iqr_str(x):
    q = np.percentile(x, [25, 50, 75])
    return f"{q[1]:.1f} (IQR {q[0]:.1f} to {q[2]:.1f})"

def emg_ratio(r, sl):
    """median EMG RMS in 1-s windows inside sl over that outside, within the recording"""
    e = r["emg"]
    if e is None or sl is None or len(sl) == 0:
        return np.nan
    t = e[:, 0]
    ins = P.overlaps(np.c_[t, t + 1.0], sl)
    ok = (t > r["t0"]) & (t + 1 < r["t1"])
    if ins[ok].sum() < 10 or (~ins[ok]).sum() < 10:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.median(e[ok & ins, 1]) / np.median(e[ok & ~ins, 1]))

EMG ratio (below 1: lower muscle tone in sleep-like time): per-probe detection 0.8 (IQR 0.8 to 0.9) | main 0.9 (IQR 0.8 to 1.0) (62 recordings with both)
probes with 0 to 74 cortical units: 24; per-probe sleep-like % 84.5 (IQR 40.8 to 99.5); its null % 33.3 (IQR 1.9 to 87.1)
probes with 75 to 149 cortical units: 14; per-probe sleep-like % 16.1 (IQR 12.4 to 29.7); its null % 0.1 (IQR 0.1 to 0.1)
probes with 150 to 999 cortical units: 36; per-probe sleep-like % 21.2 (IQR 10.7 to 32.6); its null % 0.0 (IQR 0.0 to 0.0)
sessions without detection if the null threshold were 0.1 %: 10
sessions without detection if the null threshold were 1 %: 10
sessions without detection if the null threshold were 5 %: 7
main sleep-like % where the paper used off-period detection 15.9 (IQR 7.6 to 23.7) | where it did not 3.1 (IQR 0.0 to 6.4)
Spearman r between main and the paper's quiet %, recordings with a file: 0.65

Result: not reproduced. With the main detector, sleep-like periods take a median 9.9% of a probe recording (IQR 2.7 to 20.3%) against 6% (0 to 18%); recordings hold a median 215 active epochs (227 ± 22.7, within tolerance) but 73.5 sleep-like epochs (19 expected), and 8,405 ww units have at least 12 sleep-like epochs (11,599 ± 1,160). Per session the values are similar (10.5%, 207, 73.5). No detector reading reproduces the values: per probe 20.0%, 180 and 125; the code's detector 8.7%, 203 and 83.5; even the paper's own sleep-like periods from Zenodo give 1.5%, 248 and 21.5 on these recordings. The paper's own detection files give a median quiet time of 5.3% (IQR 0.7 to 17.2%) of their recording time over 73 recordings, close to the claim, and mark 19 recordings as not using off-period detection; where the paper used it, the main detector marks a median 15.9% of the time, where it did not 3.1%, and the two agree in rank (Spearman 0.65).

The per-probe check shows why the main reading pools a session's probes: with fewer than 75 cortical units the per-probe detector marks a median 84.5% of the time, against 33.3% in a Poisson population with no off periods, while with 75 or more units the null marks 0.1% or less and the detector still marks 16 to 21%. So for well-sampled recordings the excess over 6% is in the data and the detector, not the unit count. The EMG is lower in the detected periods (median ratio 0.9, IQR 0.8 to 1.0, over 62 recordings), consistent with drowsiness, though weakly.

extfig1f-burstiness-memory-uncorrelated¶

Across ww units, a linear correlation does not reveal a dependence between burstiness and memory.

A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test: B ~ 1 + M + (1|Mouse) across all ww units (Methods, equation 8), p < 0.05.

In [13]:
ww_all = U[(U.utype == "ww") & (U.n_valid >= P.MIN_EPOCHS)].dropna(subset=["log10FR", "B", "M"]).copy()
for form in ["B ~ M", "M ~ B", "B ~ log10FR", "M ~ log10FR"]:
    f, r2 = P.mixed(ww_all, form)
    print(f"{form}: slope {f.params.iloc[1]:.4f}, p = {f.pvalues.iloc[1]:.3g}, marginal R2 = {r2:.4f}, n = {len(ww_all)}")
print("Pearson r(B, M) across ww units:", round(stats.pearsonr(ww_all.B, ww_all.M)[0], 3))

B ~ M: slope -0.1967, p = 7.03e-75, marginal R2 = 0.0252, n = 12112

M ~ B: slope -0.1372, p = 2.18e-75, marginal R2 = 0.0284, n = 12112

B ~ log10FR: slope -0.0229, p = 4.74e-15, marginal R2 = 0.0047, n = 12112

M ~ log10FR: slope 0.1090, p = 0, marginal R2 = 0.1632, n = 12112
Pearson r(B, M) across ww units: -0.173

Result: not reproduced. By the paper's test burstiness depends on memory: slope -0.197, p = 7.0e-75, across 12,112 ww units. The effect is small: marginal R2 = 0.025 (Pearson r = -0.173).

The ww and nw SOMs and their categories¶

Trained on all ww (or nw) units with at least 12 active epochs, all regions and layers (code somsettings_carlenSpont.yml: layerlist all). The code's shape rule gives a ww grid of 17 by 25 = 425 nodes from the 400 of its settings (a deviation in size only). The two readings of which retrained cluster is which category (claims file, G2) are shown with each cluster's median metrics. Reading (a) applies the code's permutation in the code's direction: relabel_clusters.py runs for newval, oldval in enumerate(sortarray): labels[labels_orig == oldval] = newval, so the cluster of memory rank sortarray[k] (0 the highest median memory, cluster_SOM.py sorting by -np.median) becomes category k + 1; pfcki.category_maps does the same.

In [14]:
fit_ww = P.fit_categories(ww_all, 400, 8)
ww_all["cat_a"], ww_all["cat_b"], ww_all["node"] = fit_ww["cat_a"], fit_ww["cat_b"], fit_ww["node"]
print("ww SOM grid", fit_ww["som"]["shape"], "=", fit_ww["som"]["W"].shape[0], "nodes (code's get_kshape rounds up from 400)")
tab = fit_ww["med"].assign(reading_a=fit_ww["map_a"], reading_b=fit_ww["map_b"],
                           units=np.bincount(fit_ww["lab"][fit_ww["node"]], minlength=8))
print(tab.sort_values("reading_b").round(3).to_string())
print("\nText: 1-3 low rate regular (1 most regular), 4-6 high rate (4 Poissonian, 6 bursty), 7-8 low rate bursty")
print("Clusters given the same number by both readings:", int((fit_ww["map_a"] == fit_ww["map_b"]).sum()), "of 8")
nw_all = U[(U.utype == "nw") & (U.n_valid >= P.MIN_EPOCHS)].dropna(subset=["log10FR", "B", "M"]).copy()
fit_nw = P.fit_categories(nw_all, 220, 5)
nw_all["cat_a"] = fit_nw["cat_a"]
print("\nnw SOM grid", fit_nw["som"]["shape"], "| clusters with the code's numbering (reading a):")
print(fit_nw["med"].assign(reading_a=fit_nw["map_a"], units=np.bincount(fit_nw["lab"][fit_nw["node"]], minlength=5)).round(3).to_string())

fig2a-som-memory-burstiness¶

On the ww SOM, burstiness and firing rate vary along perpendicular gradients, while high memory occurs only with medium to low burstiness, so high memory and high burstiness are mutually exclusive.

In [15]:
Wd = fit_ww["som"]["W"] * fit_ww["sd"] + fit_ww["mu"]
pos = fit_ww["som"]["pos"]
ang, gB, gF = P.gradient_angle(pos, Wd[:, 1], Wd[:, 0])
print(f"angle between the B and log10FR gradients: {ang:.1f} degrees (criterion 60 to 120)")
print("node prototypes: log10FR", rng_str(Wd[:, 0]), "| B", rng_str(Wd[:, 1]), "| M", rng_str(Wd[:, 2]))
q75B = np.quantile(Wd[:, 1], 0.75)
for q, lab in [(0.9, "(a) top 10%"), (0.75, "(b) top 25%")]:
    top = Wd[:, 2] >= np.quantile(Wd[:, 2], q)
    print(f"{lab} memory nodes: {top.sum()}, of which in the top quartile of node B: {(Wd[top, 1] >= q75B).sum()} "
          f"(their B {np.round(np.sort(Wd[top, 1])[-3:], 3)}, top-quartile threshold {q75B:.3f})")
print("Spearman r of node M and node B:", round(stats.spearmanr(Wd[:, 2], Wd[:, 1])[0], 3))
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.5))
for ax, j, nm in zip(axs, range(3), ["log10FR", "B", "M"]):
    sc = ax.scatter(pos[:, 0], pos[:, 1], c=Wd[:, j], marker="h", s=60, cmap="viridis"); ax.set_title(nm); plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
    ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off")
plt.show()

(a) top 10% memory nodes: 43, of which in the top quartile of node B: 4 (their B [0.079 0.083 0.098], top-quartile threshold 0.061)

Result: partially reproduced. The gradients of B and log10FR over the node grid are at 109.8 degrees, within 60 to 120 (part 1 holds). Part 2 fails under both readings: 4 of the 43 top-10% memory nodes and 24 of the 107 top-25% memory nodes lie in the top quartile of node B. Node M and node B are weakly anticorrelated (Spearman -0.166).

fig2b-pfc-regular-territory¶

PFC ww units are widely spread on the SOM, with many matching regular-firing (low burstiness) nodes and few in anti-memory territory, while units from other regions populate different territories.

In [16]:
pfc, oth = ww_all[ww_all.is_pfc], ww_all[~ww_all.is_pfc]
print(f"PFC share of the ww SOM units: {100 * ww_all.is_pfc.mean():.1f} % ({len(pfc)} of {len(ww_all)}); expected 54 ± 5.4")
mw = stats.mannwhitneyu(pfc.B, oth.B, alternative="two-sided")
print(f"median B: PFC {pfc.B.median():.4f}, other {oth.B.median():.4f}, Mann-Whitney p = {mw.pvalue:.3g}")
tabm = np.array([[(pfc.M < 0).sum(), (pfc.M >= 0).sum()], [(oth.M < 0).sum(), (oth.M >= 0).sum()]])
chi = stats.chi2_contingency(tabm)
print(f"fraction M < 0: PFC {(pfc.M < 0).mean():.3f}, other {(oth.M < 0).mean():.3f}, chi-square p = {chi[1]:.3g}")
print("nodes hit by PFC units:", pfc.node.nunique(), "of", fit_ww["som"]["W"].shape[0], "| by other units:", oth.node.nunique())
print("\nPer setting:")
print(ww_all.groupby(["setting", "is_pfc"]).agg(medB=("B", "median"), fracMneg=("M", lambda x: (x < 0).mean()), n=("B", "size")).round(3).unstack().to_string())

The fraction with M < 0 is lower in the PFC in every setting; the median B is too, except in Aversion (-0.076 against -0.096).

fig2e-category-stability¶

About 57% of ww units keep their category from one block of about 50 spontaneous epochs to the next, far above the 18% expected by chance from the marginal distributions.

Blocks: where the trials table's Block column marks runs of trials (the 6 Aversion and 14 Context files; no Opto or Passive file), each run is a block, runs of more than 75 epochs split in two; elsewhere consecutive blocks of 50 onsets (assumption, as the files do not say which recordings had an inherent block structure). Block metrics need at least 12 active epochs of at least 6 spikes (Methods); the code's minimum of 3 is a variant. Stability does not depend on which cluster is given which number, so G2 does not apply.

In [17]:
print("Block structure per file:", pd.Series([r["blockmode"] for r in recs]).value_counts().to_dict(),
      "| blocks per file:", rng_str([len(np.unique(r["blocks"])) for r in recs]))
bc = P.block_categories(recs, ww_all, fit_ww)
print("unit-blocks:", len(bc), "| units with at least one block:", bc.groupby(["session", "unit_id"]).ngroups,
      "| epochs per analysed block (median, IQR):", np.percentile(bc.n_epochs, [50, 25, 75]))
Ms = P.transitions(bc, "cat_b", 8)
st_t = pd.DataFrame([{"transition": t, "units": int(M.sum()), "stability": P.stability(M)[0], "chance": P.stability(M)[1]}
                     for t, M in Ms.items()])
print(st_t.round(3).to_string(index=False))
Msum = sum(Ms.values())
print(f"(a) mean over transitions: stability {st_t.stability.mean():.3f}, chance {st_t.chance.mean():.3f}")
print(f"(b) pooled matrix: stability {P.stability(Msum)[0]:.3f}, chance {P.stability(Msum)[1]:.3f}")
print("expected 0.57 ± 0.057 and 0.18 ± 0.018")
bc3 = P.block_categories(recs, ww_all, fit_ww, min_valid=3)
Ms3 = P.transitions(bc3, "cat_b", 8)
s3 = [P.stability(M) for M in Ms3.values()]
print(f"\nVariant, blocks with >= 3 valid epochs: mean {np.mean([s[0] for s in s3]):.3f} (chance {np.mean([s[1] for s in s3]):.3f}),"
      f" pooled {P.stability(sum(Ms3.values()))[0]:.3f}")
bcs = bc.merge(ww_all[["session", "unit_id", "setting"]], on=["session", "unit_id"])
print("\nPooled stability by setting:")
for sname, g in bcs.groupby("setting"):
    Mg = sum(P.transitions(g, "cat_b", 8).values())
    if np.sum(Mg) > 0:
        print(f"  {sname}: {P.stability(Mg)[0]:.3f} (chance {P.stability(Mg)[1]:.3f}, {int(Mg.sum())} transitions)")

Result: reproduced (with the block structure assumed). Units keep their category from one block to the next in 58.0% of transitions on average over 13 transitions (reading a), against 16.7% expected from the marginals, both within tolerance (57 ± 5.7, 18 ± 1.8); the pooled matrix gives 58.5% against 16.0% (reading b), the chance level just below 16.2. Per transition the stability lies between 54.3% and 60.9%. With the code's minimum of 3 valid epochs per block it is 50.4% (chance 14.8%). Blocks keep a median 27 valid epochs (IQR 18 to 37).

fig2f-low-rate-less-stable¶

Block-wise category assignment is less stable for low-rate categories (1 to 3, 7 and 8) than for high-rate categories, and low-rate regular categories 1 to 3 mostly transition among themselves, as do the low-rate bursty categories 7 and 8.

In [18]:
def fig2f_parts(bc_, cat):
    M = sum(P.transitions(bc_, cat, 8).values())
    Pm = M / M.sum(1, keepdims=True)
    X = P.coincidence(M)
    low, high = [0, 1, 2, 6, 7], [3, 4, 5]
    d, dx = np.diag(Pm), np.diag(X)
    part1 = d[low].mean() < d[high].mean()
    part1x = dx[low].mean() < dx[high].mean()
    part2 = []
    for grp in ([0, 1, 2], [6, 7]):
        for i in grp:
            others = [j for j in grp if j != i]
            out = [j for j in range(8) if j not in grp]
            part2.append(Pm[i, others].sum() > Pm[i, out].max())
    return Pm, X, d, dx, part1, part1x, part2

for cat in ["cat_a", "cat_b"]:
    Pm, X, d, dx, p1, p1x, p2 = fig2f_parts(bc, cat)
    print(f"G2 reading {cat[-1]}: diagonal of P by category 1..8: {np.round(d, 3)}")
    print(f"   mean diagonal low-rate (1-3,7,8) {d[[0,1,2,6,7]].mean():.3f} vs high-rate (4-6) {d[[3,4,5]].mean():.3f} -> part 1 {p1};"
          f" coincidence diagonal {np.round(dx, 3)} -> {p1x}")
    print(f"   part 2 (within-group probability above any single outside category), categories 1,2,3,7,8: {p2}")
    print(pd.DataFrame(Pm, index=range(1, 9), columns=range(1, 9)).round(2).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced, under both G2 readings. Part 1 holds: the mean diagonal of P is 0.520 for categories 1 to 3, 7 and 8 against 0.575 for 4 to 6 under G2 a, and 0.444 against 0.702 under G2 b, and the coincidence diagonal agrees. Part 2 fails: within-group transitions exceed any single outside category for categories 1, 2 and 3 under both readings, but not for 7 and 8 (G2 a) or 7 (G2 b). With the paper's own sleep-like periods (variant before the summary) the outcome is the same.

Region enrichment of ww categories¶

Deep-layer units for cortical regions and all units elsewhere, against all such units (the code's refall), PFC subregions and the code's parent regions, regions with more than 20 units, 1,000 shuffles within each behavioral setting. G1: (a) five groups, Opto merged into Passive (code); (b) six settings. Both G2 readings. An E-score is called significant when its count lies above the 95th or below the 5th percentile of the shuffles (claims header, from the code), so "P < 0.05" here is a 5% test in each tail, a 10% test two-sided.

In [19]:

print("units:", len(sel), "| regions with more than 20 units:", len(regs))

                             pops=list(regs) + ["other"], attrs=range(1, 9))
        ENR[(g1, g2)] = (E.loc[regs], Pv.loc[regs])
show = ["ILA", "PL", "ACAd", "ACAv", "ORBm", "ORBvl", "ORBl", "MOs", "AIv", "AId", "FRP", "TH", "HPF"]

          E.loc[[r for r in show if r in E.index]].round(1).astype(str) + "*").to_string())

Result: reproduced. All six subregions are enriched in categories 1 to 3 under both readings of "generally enriched", both groupings and both G2 readings: the sums of their E-scores are 1.6 to 9.9, and each has a significant positive E-score in at least one of the three categories. With the paper's own sleep-like periods (variant before the summary) five of six meet reading (a) under G2 a, so the outcome would differ under G2: it depends on the detector.

extfig3f-layer-enrichment¶

Superficial cortical layers (L2/3) are enriched in bursty ww units, while deep layers (L5 to 6) are enriched in regular-firing ww units.

Result: partially reproduced, under both G1 and both G2 readings. L2/3 is significantly enriched in bursty categories (G2 a: 6 and 7, E = 4.0 to 4.2; G2 b: 6 and 8, 1.8 to 4.0) and L6 in a regular category (category 2, E = 2.4 to 2.6), but L5 has no significant positive E-score in categories 1 to 3 (at most 1.5). Two of the three parts hold. With the paper's own sleep-like periods (variant before the summary) the outcome is the same.

extfig5g-nw-enrichment¶

Among nw units, ILA, PL and ACAd/v are significantly enriched in high-rate, regular-firing units with high memory, and ORBl in high-rate, bursty units.

The regular high-memory nw category is the one with median log10FR above the median over all nw units and the lowest median B; the bursty one has median log10FR above that median and the highest median B (claims file, by category medians).

Result: partially reproduced. By category medians the regular high-memory nw category is 2 (median log10FR 1.237, B 0.003, M 0.073) and the bursty one 1 (0.946, 0.170, 0.074); only these two lie above the median log10FR of nw units (0.658), so the two picks are complements, and their median M is nearly equal. ILA (E = 2.1 to 2.2) and ACAv (2.9 to 3.0) are significantly enriched in category 2 but PL is not (-1.2), so part 1 fails; ORBl is significantly enriched in category 1 (1.9), so part 2 holds, under both groupings. With the paper's own sleep-like periods (variant before the summary) neither part holds (not reproduced): the outcome depends on the detector.

fig2j-nw-ww-correspondence¶

Brain (sub)regions enriched in low-rate, regular-firing ww units are enriched in high-rate, regular-firing nw units, and regions enriched in low-rate bursty ww units are enriched in high-rate bursty nw units.

Result: not reproduced. Across 21 regions with more than 20 nw units (9 in the paper), the mean correlation between the E-scores of ww categories 1 to 3 and of the regular nw category is -0.070 to -0.025, not positive, under every reading. The mean correlation between ww categories 7 and 8 and the bursty nw category is positive (0.016 to 0.264). Over the 9 regions with the most nw units the first is -0.131 to 0.002 and the second -0.157 to 0.215, negative under G2 a. The regular part fails under every reading and the bursty part depends on the region set and G2.

Harris hierarchy (Fig. 3)¶

The Harris et al. 2019 scores as the code reads them. Populations are the cortical areas with a score (deep layers), all other units form one rest population (code harris_vs_enrichment.py); E-scores grouped by setting (Methods), and without groups as the code's Fig. 3 script does (variant). Areas with more than 20 units.

fig3a-harris-regular-positive¶

In dataset KI, enrichment of cortical (sub)regions in low-rate, regular-firing units (categories 1 to 3, category 2 shown) correlates positively with the Harris cortical hierarchy score, driven by the split between low-hierarchy sensory regions and high-hierarchy PFC subregions.

In [28]:
def harris_r(E, cats, areas=None):
    a = areasH if areas is None else areas
    return {c: stats.pearsonr(harris[a], E.loc[a, c]) for c in cats}

for key, (E, Pv) in HAR.items():
    rr = harris_r(E, [1, 2, 3])
    ok = rr[2][0] > 0 and rr[2][1] < 0.05 and rr[1][0] > 0 and rr[3][0] > 0
    part = rr[2][0] > 0 and rr[2][1] < 0.05
    print(f"{key}: r1 {rr[1][0]:.2f} (p {rr[1][1]:.3f}), r2 {rr[2][0]:.2f} (p {rr[2][1]:.3f}), r3 {rr[3][0]:.2f} (p {rr[3][1]:.3f})"
          f" -> all {ok}, category 2 alone {part}")
E, _ = HAR[("G1 a", "b")]
pf = [a for a in areasH if a in P.PFC_SUBREGIONS]
print("\nG1 a, G2 b: mean category 2 E-score, PFC areas", round(E.loc[pf, 2].mean(), 2), "| other areas",
      round(E.loc[[a for a in areasH if a not in pf], 2].mean(), 2), "| Harris score PFC", round(harris[pf].mean(), 3),
      "other", round(harris[[a for a in areasH if a not in pf]].mean(), 3))

('no groups', 'b'): r1 0.14 (p 0.611), r2 0.64 (p 0.007), r3 -0.02 (p 0.949) -> all False, category 2 alone True

G1 a, G2 b: mean category 2 E-score, PFC areas 4.11 | other areas -2.07 | Harris score PFC 0.261 other -0.082

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). Across 16 cortical areas with a Harris score and more than 20 deep ww units (17 in the paper), category 2 enrichment correlates positively with hierarchy under every reading (r = 0.61, p = 0.012 with groups; 0.64, p = 0.007 without). Categories 1 and 3 are positive as well under G2 b (r = 0.20 and 0.02 to 0.04): reproduced. Under G2 a category 1 is negative (r = -0.12 to -0.14): partially reproduced. The outcome differs under G2. PFC areas have higher category 2 E-scores (4.11) and Harris scores (0.261) than the other areas (-2.07, -0.082). With the paper's own SOM (variant) categories 1 to 3 are all positive and category 2 significant (r = 0.55 to 0.57, p ≤ 0.026). With the paper's own sleep-like periods (variant before the summary) the outcome still differs under G2 (category 2 r = 0.56 under G2 b, -0.35 to -0.32 under G2 a).

supptable5-no-hierarchy-within-pfc¶

zenodo-unit-link¶

Link claim (the registry's): the paper's per-unit metrics files on Zenodo can be matched to the dataset's units, and the matched records agree on what both describe.

Records are matched by recording id and unit id. Agreement is checked on the location (area and layer), the peak-to-trough duration, and the ww/nw label against the Methods thresholds applied to the dataset's Peak_to_Trough. The files' quality flags are compared with the paper's count of units kept.

fig4b-dataroi-parcellation¶

The PFC flatmap is parcellated into 42 dataROIs that respect subregion boundaries, each holding about 200 deep-layer ww units.

Deep-layer PFC ww units with at least 12 active epochs and a flatmap position, assigned to a subregion by the subregion polygon that contains them (code flatmap_tessellation.py); the dataset's location label is shown as a check. Size bounds 160 to 240 (Methods), 180 to 220 as a variant (code).

fig4cd-dataroi-enrichment¶

Low-rate, regular-firing categories 1 and 3 are significantly enriched in dataROIs in ILA and PL, while low-rate, bursty categories 7 and 8 are enriched in dataROIs in MOs and ORBl, the ORBl enrichment pinpointed to its most ventral dataROI.

Reference (a) all deep PFC ww units of the parcellation; (b) all units as for regions (the dataROIs plus one rest population of every other unit of the region analysis). Groups by setting (G1 a and b), both G2 readings, dataROIs from the 160-240 parcellation.

In [33]:
def droi_escores(fm_, roicol, ref, g1, g2, seed, pool=None):
    """E-scores per ROI; reference (a) the PFC units of fm_, (b) these and the rest of pool (default sel)"""
    pool = sel if pool is None else pool
    if ref == "a":
        pops, cats = fm_[roicol].values, fm_["cat_" + g2].values
        grp = fm_.setting.replace({"Opto": "Passive"}).values if g1 == "a" else fm_.setting.values
        plist = sorted(pd.unique(pops))
    else:
        rest = pool[~pool.set_index(["session", "unit_id"]).index.isin(fm_.set_index(["session", "unit_id"]).index)]
        both = pd.concat([fm_.assign(pp=fm_[roicol]), rest.assign(pp="rest")])
        pops, cats = both.pp.values, both["cat_" + g2].values
        grp = both.setting.replace({"Opto": "Passive"}).values if g1 == "a" else both.setting.values
        plist = sorted(pd.unique(fm_[roicol])) + ["rest"]
    E, Pv, _ = P.escore(pops, cats, grp, 1000, seed=seed, pops=plist, attrs=range(1, 9))
    keep = [p for p in plist if p != "rest"]
    return E.loc[keep], Pv.loc[keep]

DROI = {}
for ref in ["a", "b"]:
    for g1 in ["a", "b"]:
        for g2 in ["a", "b"]:
            E, Pv = droi_escores(fm, "droi", ref, g1, g2, seed=21)
            DROI[(ref, g1, g2)] = (E, Pv)
            sp = (E > 0) & (Pv < 0.05)
            sub = lambda r, cs: any(sp.loc[i, cs].any() for i in E.index if i.startswith(r + "-"))
            ok = sub("ILA", [1, 3]) and sub("PL", [1, 3]) and sub("MOs", [7, 8]) and sub("ORBl", [7, 8])
            orbl = [i for i in E.index if i.startswith("ORBl-")]
            best = E.loc[orbl, [7, 8]].sum(1).idxmax() if orbl else None
            print(f"reference {ref}, G1 {g1}, G2 {g2}: ILA 1/3 {sub('ILA', [1, 3])}, PL 1/3 {sub('PL', [1, 3])}, "
                  f"MOs 7/8 {sub('MOs', [7, 8])}, ORBl 7/8 {sub('ORBl', [7, 8])} -> {ok}; ORBl dataROI with the highest 7+8 E-score: {best}")
E, Pv = DROI[("a", "a", "b")]
print("\nreference a, G1 a, G2 b (* P < 0.05):")
print(E.round(1).astype(str).where(Pv >= 0.05, E.round(1).astype(str) + "*").to_string())

ORBl is a single dataROI here (386 units), so whether the enrichment is in its most ventral part is not tested.

fig4e-activity-modules¶

Clustering dataROIs by enrichment profile gives activity modules; ILA forms a homogeneous ILA-specific module bordering a similar module in adjacent PL and ACAd, while other modules cross cytoarchitectural boundaries and occur in several places.

Main: the 24 dataROIs of 001260 (fig4b). Two variants, asked for in review: (1) the paper's own 42 dataROI polygons from Zenodo (flatmap_PFC_ntesselated_obeyRegions_res200.h5), each holding the 001260 units inside it and named by the subregion of most of its units, those with at least 20 units; (2) all of dataset KI, the 001260 units plus the 000473 deep PFC ww units projected on the ww SOM trained here (their metrics as for 001260), parcellated as in fig4b, reference (a).

from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import fcluster, linkage
for key, (E, Pv) in DROI.items():
    Zs = (E - E.mean(0)) / E.std(0)
    mod = pd.Series(fcluster(linkage(Zs.values, "ward"), 5, "maxclust"), index=E.index)
    subr = mod.index.str.split("-").str[0]
    ila = mod[subr == "ILA"]
    one = ila.nunique() == 1
    m_ila = ila.iloc[0] if one else None
    rd_a = one and (subr[mod == m_ila] == "ILA").all()
    rd_b = one and (subr[mod == m_ila] == "ILA").mean() > 0.5
    multi = sum(len(set(subr[mod == m])) > 1 for m in mod.unique() if m != m_ila)
    print(f"ref {key[0]} G1 {key[1]} G2 {key[2]}: ILA dataROIs {len(ila)} in one module {one}; ILA-only (a) {rd_a}, "
          f"mostly ILA (b) {rd_b}; other modules spanning subregions {multi}")
    if key == ("a", "a", "b"):
        print(pd.crosstab(mod.values, subr, rownames=["module"], colnames=["subregion"]).to_string())

def module_check(E, k=5):
    Zs = (E - E.mean(0)) / E.std(0).replace(0, 1)
    mod = pd.Series(fcluster(linkage(Zs.fillna(0).values, "ward"), k, "maxclust"), index=E.index)
    subr = mod.index.str.split("-").str[0]
    ila = mod[subr == "ILA"]
    one = ila.nunique() == 1
    m_ila = ila.iloc[0] if one else None
    rd_a = bool(one and (subr[mod == m_ila] == "ILA").all())
    rd_b = bool(one and (subr[mod == m_ila] == "ILA").mean() > 0.5)
    multi = sum(len(set(subr[mod == m])) > 1 for m in mod.unique() if m != m_ila)
    comp = pd.Series(subr[mod == m_ila]).value_counts().to_dict() if one else None
    return len(ila), one, rd_a, rd_b, multi, comp, mod

Result: blocked (methods underspecified), as the claim's two readings of "ILA-specific" disagree. The two ILA dataROIs of 001260 fall in one module under every reading, and three or four other modules hold dataROIs of several subregions. With reference (b) that module holds only the ILA dataROIs (both readings hold); with reference (a) and G1 a it also holds a MOs dataROI, so it is mostly ILA (b) but not ILA-only (a); with reference (a) and G1 b neither holds. The variants with finer parcellations do not support an ILA-specific module: on the paper's 42 dataROIs the 4 ILA dataROIs are split (reference a) or share a module with 4 to 5 PL, 3 MOs and 3 ORBm dataROIs (reference b), and on all of dataset KI (39 dataROIs) the 3 ILA dataROIs share a module with 3 or 4 PL and one ORBm dataROI. With the paper's own SOM (variant at the end) the module of the 2 ILA dataROIs holds only ILA under every reference and grouping. With the paper's own sleep-like periods (variant before the summary) the readings still disagree: the ILA module holds one PL dataROI under every reading.

GaoROIs and the intra-PFC hierarchy (Fig. 4g,h, Extended Data Fig. 7n)¶

Units are assigned to the 60 GaoROI polygons (Zenodo flatmap_PFCrois.h5); GaoROIs with at least 20 deep ww units (Extended Data Fig. 7i; more than 20 as a variant) and a hierarchy score. E-scores as for dataROIs (both references, G1, G2), Pearson correlation with the Gao hierarchy index.

gh = gao_h = P.gao_hierarchy()

gcount = fm.groi.value_counts()
print("deep PFC ww units in a GaoROI:", int(fm.groi.notna().sum()), "of", len(fm), "| GaoROIs with units:", len(gcount),
      "| with >= 20:", int((gcount >= 20).sum()), "| with >= 20 and a score:", int(((gcount >= 20) & gcount.index.isin(gh.dropna().index)).sum()),
      "| with > 20 and a score:", int(((gcount > 20) & gcount.index.isin(gh.dropna().index)).sum()), "(paper 30)")
GAO = {}
for nmin_lab, keep in [(">= 20", gcount[gcount >= 20].index), ("> 20", gcount[gcount > 20].index)]:
    keep = [int(k) for k in keep if k in gh.dropna().index]
    fg = fm[fm.groi.isin(keep)].copy()
    fg["groi_s"] = fg.groi.astype(int).astype(str)
    for ref in ["a", "b"]:
        for g1 in ["a", "b"]:
            for g2 in ["a", "b"]:

                E.index = E.index.astype(int); Pv.index = Pv.index.astype(int)
                GAO[(nmin_lab, ref, g1, g2)] = (E, Pv)
for key, (E, Pv) in GAO.items():
    h = gh[E.index]
    r1, r6 = stats.pearsonr(h, E[1]), stats.pearsonr(h, E[6])
    print(f"n {key[0]}, ref {key[1]}, G1 {key[2]}, G2 {key[3]}: {len(E)} GaoROIs; category 1 r = {r1[0]:.2f} (p {r1[1]:.3f}),"
          f" category 6 r = {r6[0]:.2f} (p {r6[1]:.3f})")

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). Across 29 GaoROIs (30 in the paper), category 1 enrichment correlates with the Gao hierarchy index positively under G2 b (r = 0.39 to 0.40, p 0.030 to 0.034 with reference a, reproduced; r = 0.28 to 0.29, p ≥ 0.125 with reference b) and negatively under G2 a (r = -0.33 to -0.38, p 0.044 to 0.078). The outcome differs under G2. With the paper's own SOM (variant) r = 0.34 to 0.36, p 0.055 to 0.069. With the paper's own sleep-like periods (variant before the summary) r = 0.04 to 0.27 (p ≥ 0.160) under every reading, which is not reproduced: the outcome depends on the detector.

In the Gao table GaoROI 23 has the lowest score of the 29 analysed, but 19, 20 and 41 rank 6th, 8th and 11th (the highest three are 5, 24 and 2), so their "exceptionally high" scores are not in the table under these IDs (asked of a reader). Under G2 a none of 19, 20 and 41 is in the top three and 23 is not the lowest: not reproduced. The outcome differs between readings. With the paper's own SOM (variant) 20 and 41 are in the top three under every reading, and 23 is the lowest in one of four.

Tone responses (Fig. 5b, 5j)¶

Tone response traces as in the Methods (pfcki.tone_traces): 10-kHz tones only (the working-memory recordings have none and are left out), epochs with licking, sleep-like periods or saturation dropped, units below 0.1 Hz overall or before the tone dropped, PCA over ww and nw units pooled, 8 components. A SOM of 400 nodes on ww units, trained on (a) deep-layer ww units of all regions (Results) or (b) all ww units (code); Ward into 8 categories numbered by the peak latency of their mean trace, the category with the lowest mean peak last (Methods: "the flat or negative category last").

In [40]:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
trecs = [r for r in recs if r["tones"] is not None]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    TT = list(ex.map(P.tone_traces, trecs))
T = pd.concat([pd.DataFrame({"session": r["session"], "unit_id": r["units"].unit_id.values, "rate_all": o["rate_all"],
                             "rate_pre": o["rate_pre"], "n_tone_epochs": o["n_tones"]}) for r, o in zip(trecs, TT)], ignore_index=True)
X = np.vstack([o["trace"] for o in TT])
T = T.merge(U[["session", "unit_id", "utype", "is_pfc", "deep", "area", "region", "setting", "subject", "cortical"]], on=["session", "unit_id"])
print("files with 10-kHz tones:", len(trecs), "| tone response epochs per file:", rng_str([o["n_tones"] for o in TT]),
      "(paper: 188, IQR 86 to 228)")
okT = ((T.rate_all >= 0.1) & (T.rate_pre >= 0.1) & np.isfinite(X).all(1) & T.utype.isin(["ww", "nw"])).values
print("units:", len(T), "| kept (rates >= 0.1 Hz, ww or nw):", int(okT.sum()))
T, X = T[okT].reset_index(drop=True), X[okT]
Xc = X - X.mean(0)
w, V = np.linalg.eigh(np.cov(Xc.T))
o = np.argsort(w)[::-1][:8]
pcs = V[:, o].T
print(f"variance explained by 8 components: {w[o].sum() / w.sum():.3f} (Methods: over 95%)")
Sc = X @ pcs.T
tt = np.arange(X.shape[1]) * P.PSTH_BIN
TONE = {}
for rd, m in [("a", ((T.utype == "ww") & ((~T.cortical) | T.deep)).values), ("b", (T.utype == "ww").values)]:
    Z0 = Sc[m]
    Zs = (Z0 - Z0.mean(0)) / Z0.std(0)
    som_t = P.train_som(Zs, 400)
    lab = P.ward_clusters(som_t["W"], 8)
    cl = lab[P.bmus(Zs, som_t["W"])]
    mt = np.array([X[m][cl == c].mean(0) for c in range(8)])
    peak, lat = mt.max(1), tt[mt.argmax(1)]
    flat = int(np.argmin(peak))
    order = [c for c in np.argsort(lat) if c != flat] + [flat]
    num = np.zeros(8, int)
    for i, c in enumerate(order):
        num[c] = i + 1
    D = T[m].copy()
    D["tcat"] = num[cl]
    TONE[rd] = D
    pf = D[D.is_pfc & D.deep]
    print(f"\nreading {rd}: {m.sum()} ww units trained, {len(pf)} PFC deep ww units (paper 7,184 for all of dataset KI)")
    print(pd.DataFrame({"category": num, "mean peak (z)": peak.round(2), "peak latency (ms)": (lat * 1000).round(1),
                        "units": np.bincount(cl, minlength=8), "PFC deep ww": [int((pf.tcat == num[c]).sum()) for c in range(8)]}
                       ).sort_values("category").to_string(index=False))
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3))
for ax, rd in zip(axs, ["a", "b"]):
    D = TONE[rd]
    for c in range(1, 9):
        sel_ = (T.set_index(["session", "unit_id"]).index.isin(D[D.tcat == c].set_index(["session", "unit_id"]).index))
        ax.plot(tt * 1000, X[sel_].mean(0), label=str(c))
    ax.set_title(f"reading {rd}: mean trace per category"); ax.set_xlabel("ms after tone"); ax.set_ylabel("z")
axs[1].legend(ncol=4, fontsize=7)
plt.show()

fig5b-tone-categories¶

Deep-layer PFC ww tone responses cluster into eight categories ordered by peak delay; most units have flat or negative responses (category 8), categories 1 to 4 have sharp peaks with consistent onsets, and categories 5 to 7 have variable onsets and persistent responses.

ZETA test (pfcki.zeta_unit) on the PFC deep ww units of categories 1 to 7 under either reading; the spread of onsets is the IQR over units with P < 0.01.

In [41]:
import multiprocessing as mp
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
# all PFC deep ww units with a tone trace (needed for fig5e as well)
need = TONE["b"][TONE["b"].is_pfc & TONE["b"].deep][["session", "unit_id"]].drop_duplicates()
by_s = {r["session"]: r for r in trecs}
args, keys = [], []
for s, g in need.groupby("session"):
    a = P.zeta_for(by_s[s], g.unit_id.values, seed=5)
    args += a
    keys += [(s, u) for u in g.unit_id.values]
t0 = time.time()
with ProcessPoolExecutor(4, mp_context=mp.get_context("fork")) as ex:
    zres = list(ex.map(P.zeta_unit, args, chunksize=8))
ZT = pd.DataFrame(keys, columns=["session", "unit_id"]).assign(zeta_p=[z[0] for z in zres], onset=[z[1] for z in zres])
print(f"ZETA on {len(ZT)} units in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s; failed or empty: {int(ZT.zeta_p.isna().sum())}")
for rd in "ab":
    D = TONE[rd][TONE[rd].is_pfc & TONE[rd].deep].merge(ZT, on=["session", "unit_id"], how="left")
    cnt = D.tcat.value_counts().sort_index()
    largest = cnt.idxmax() == 8
    rows = []
    for c in range(1, 8):
        g = D[(D.tcat == c) & (D.zeta_p < 0.01)]
        q = np.percentile(g.onset.dropna(), [25, 50, 75]) * 1000 if len(g.onset.dropna()) >= 3 else [np.nan] * 3
        rows.append({"category": c, "units": int((D.tcat == c).sum()), "ZETA P < 0.01": len(g),
                     "onset median (ms)": round(q[1], 1), "onset IQR (ms)": round(q[2] - q[0], 1)})
    R = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    iqr = R.set_index("category")["onset IQR (ms)"]
    part2 = iqr.loc[1:4].max() < iqr.loc[5:7].min()
    print(f"\nreading {rd}: category 8 is the largest: {largest} ({cnt.get(8, 0)} of {len(D)} units)")
    print(R.to_string(index=False))
    print(f"largest IQR in 1-4: {iqr.loc[1:4].max():.1f} ms, smallest IQR in 5-7: {iqr.loc[5:7].min():.1f} ms -> part 2 {part2}")

Result: reproduced. Under both training readings the flat or negative category 8 is the largest among the 5,269 PFC deep ww units (3,837 and 3,019). The across-unit IQR of ZETA onsets of responsive units is 4.9 to 25.1 ms (reading a) or 5.4 to 43.2 ms (b) in categories 1 to 4, and 49.0 to 238.5 ms or 106.1 to 244.1 ms in categories 5 to 7. Recordings keep a median 139 tone epochs (188 in the paper); 37 of 5,269 units had too few for ZETA.

fig5cd-tone-maps-cross-subregions¶

Tone-response enrichment maps of the PFC do not follow cytoarchitectural boundaries; the earliest-responding units (category 1) are enriched in anterior ACAd and ORBvl and parts of PL, and tone response modules reveal heterogeneity within subregions.

dataROIs of fig4b; units are the PFC deep ww units with a tone category; E-scores of tone category per dataROI grouped by setting, reference (a) these units, (b) all ww units with a tone category in the region analysis (deep cortical and all non-cortical); Ward of the standardized profiles into 4 modules (Extended Data Fig. 8e). Both tone readings. As a variant, the paper's own 42 dataROI polygons (fig4e, variant 1).

In [42]:
for rd in "ab":
    D = TONE[rd]
    ft = fm.merge(D[["session", "unit_id", "tcat"]], on=["session", "unit_id"])
    reg_all = D[(~D.cortical) | D.deep]
    for ref in "ab":
        for g1 in "ab":
            if ref == "a":
                pops, cats, sett, plist = ft.droi.values, ft.tcat.values, ft.setting, sorted(ft.droi.unique())
            else:
                rest = reg_all[~reg_all.set_index(["session", "unit_id"]).index.isin(ft.set_index(["session", "unit_id"]).index)]
                both = pd.concat([ft.assign(pp=ft.droi), rest.assign(pp="rest")])
                pops, cats, sett, plist = both.pp.values, both.tcat.values, both.setting, sorted(ft.droi.unique()) + ["rest"]
            grp = sett.replace({"Opto": "Passive"}).values if g1 == "a" else sett.values
            E, Pv, _ = P.escore(pops, cats, grp, 1000, seed=51, pops=plist, attrs=range(1, 9))
            E, Pv = E.loc[sorted(ft.droi.unique())], Pv.loc[sorted(ft.droi.unique())]
            sp1 = (E[1] > 0) & (Pv[1] < 0.05)
            subr = E.index.str.split("-").str[0]
            hit = {r: bool(sp1[subr == r].any()) for r in ["ACAd", "ORBvl", "PL"]}
            Zs = (E - E.mean(0)) / E.std(0).replace(0, 1)
            mod = pd.Series(fcluster(linkage(Zs.fillna(0).values, "ward"), 4, "maxclust"), index=E.index)
            split = [r for r in pd.unique(subr) if mod[subr == r].nunique() > 1]
            print(f"tone {rd}, ref {ref}, G1 {g1}: {len(ft)} units; category 1 enriched dataROI in ACAd/ORBvl/PL {hit};"
                  f" subregions whose dataROIs fall in more than one module: {split} -> {all(hit.values()) and len(split) >= 2}")
            if rd == "a" and ref == "a" and g1 == "a":
                print(E.round(1).astype(str).where(Pv >= 0.05, E.round(1).astype(str) + "*").assign(module=mod.values).to_string())

    grp = fz.setting.replace({"Opto": "Passive"}).values if g1 == "a" else fz.setting.values
    E, Pv, _ = P.escore(fz.droi.values, fz.resp.values, grp, 1000, seed=61, attrs=["responsive", "non"])
    ZETAE[g1] = (E, Pv)
    e, p = E["responsive"], Pv["responsive"]
    subr = e.index.str.split("-").str[0]
    enr, dep = (e > 0) & (p < 0.05), (e < 0) & (p < 0.05)
    both = [r for r in pd.unique(subr) if enr[subr == r].any() and dep[subr == r].any()]
    print(f"G1 {g1}: enriched dataROIs {list(e.index[enr])} in {subr[enr].nunique()} subregions; depleted {list(e.index[dep])};"
          f" subregions with both: {both} -> {subr[enr].nunique() >= 3 and len(both) >= 1}")
print(pd.DataFrame({"E": ZETAE["a"][0]["responsive"].round(2), "P": ZETAE["a"][1]["responsive"].round(3),
                    "units": fz.droi.value_counts()}).to_string())

Result: reproduced. 1,903 of 4,036 PFC deep ww units are tone-responsive (47.2%). Significantly enriched dataROIs lie in 6 (G1 a) or 7 (G1 b) subregions, and ACAd and MOs (and PL under G1 a) each hold both an enriched and a depleted dataROI. On the paper's 42 dataROIs the enriched ones lie in 5 or 6 subregions, and ACAd, MOs and ORBvl hold both.

extfig9e-tone-responsive-no-hierarchy¶

Enrichment in tone-responsive units does not correlate with intra-PFC hierarchy across GaoROIs.

A claim of absence: Pearson correlation of the GaoROI E-scores of ZETA-responsive units with the Gao hierarchy index, GaoROIs with at least 20 units and a score, p < 0.05.

fig5i-map-similarity¶

No pair of PFC maps is strongly congruent, but the choice-tuning map is most similar to the spontaneous category 1 map, the feedback-tuning map to the category 6 map, and the tone-responsiveness map to the category 8 map.

Dataset part only (the choice and feedback maps need dataset IBL, not tested). Each map is rasterized on the flatmap (pixels of 2 flatmap units, a standard choice), each pixel taking the E-score of its dataROI; cosine similarity between the tone-responsiveness map (fig5e, G1 a and b) and each spontaneous category map (fig4cd, reference a, same G1), both G2 readings. As a variant, the same on the paper's own 42 dataROI polygons (fig4e, variant 1).

Result: blocked (too large), because the claim depends on fig5g-tuned-unit-counts (dataset IBL), which is blocked. The dataset part, as computed on the 24 dataROIs of 001260, is not reproduced: the tone-responsiveness map is most similar to spontaneous category 6 (G2 a) or 3 (G2 b), and its cosine with category 8 is -0.13 to 0.12. On the paper's 42 dataROIs, category 8 has the highest cosine in one of four readings (G1 a, G2 b, 0.19) and categories 7, 6 and 3 in the others. No pair is strongly congruent: no cosine exceeds 0.23. The choice and feedback parts need dataset IBL and were not tested.

fig5j-tone-responsive-high-rate¶

At the single-unit level, tone-responsive units (tone categories 1 to 7) are more often than expected high-rate spontaneous units (categories 4 to 6), and units without clear positive tone responses (category 8) tend to have low spontaneous rates (categories 1 to 3, 7 and 8).

Mutual enrichment: spontaneous category as population, tone category as attribute, PFC deep ww units with both, 1,000 shuffles grouped by setting (G1 a, b); the code's grouping by region and setting as a variant. Both tone readings and both G2 readings.

Result: not reproduced. The criterion fails under all 12 readings. Under G2 a the summed E-score of tone categories 1 to 7 is negative in spontaneous category 6 (-9.1 to -7.5). Under G2 b it is negative in spontaneous category 4 in five readings (-4.6 to -0.2); in the sixth (tone reading a, G1 a) it is positive in 4, 5 and 6, but tone category 8 has a positive E-score in only 3 of the 5 low-rate spontaneous categories (four required). 4,123 PFC deep ww units have both categories (6,681 ± 668 expected for all of dataset KI).

methods-settings-no-difference (variant only)¶

Firing metric distributions do not differ significantly across behavioral settings.

The paper names no test; the claim is blocked. As a variant only, a mixed model Metric ~ 1 + Setting + (1|Mouse) per metric for ww units, with the size of the setting effects.

Variant: the paper's own trained ww SOM (G2)¶

The claims file allows, as a variant only, projecting units onto the paper's own trained SOM (Zenodo SOMs.zip, run runC00dMP3_brain, 17 by 24 nodes, features standardized with its stored means and s.d.), whose nodes carry the paper's category numbers (clustering_resorted/ward/8). Each ww unit of 001260 takes the category of its best matching node there (G2 z). This shows which of the two readings of G2 matches the paper's numbering on these units, and what the claims blocked under G2 give with the paper's numbering. It decides no outcome.

        print(f"dataROI modules, ref {ref}, G1 {g1}, G2 z: ILA dataROIs {n_ila} in one module {one}; ILA-only {rd_a}, mostly ILA {rd_b};"
              f" ILA module {comp}; other modules spanning subregions {multi}")

On the paper's own SOM the eight categories of these units have the medians the text describes: 1 to 3 low-rate and regular (median B -0.196 to -0.059), 4 to 6 high-rate (median log10FR 0.674 to 0.990, 6 the burstiest), 7 and 8 low-rate bursty. Neither reading of G2 reproduces the paper's numbering unit by unit: 19.9% of units get the same number under reading (a), 27.7% under (b). Under the paper's numbering, fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment, fig2g-ila-pl-category1, fig2g-bursty-orbl-mos-aiv, fig3a-harris-regular-positive and fig3c-harris-bursty-negative hold; fig2g-th-hpf-bursty holds under its reading (b) only; extfig3f-layer-enrichment holds in part (L5 not enriched); fig4g-pl-orbl-extremes in part (GaoROIs 20 and 41 in the top three); the two ILA dataROIs form an ILA-only module (fig4e); the Gao correlations are not significant (category 1 r = 0.34 to 0.36, p 0.055 to 0.069; category 6 r = -0.24 to -0.19).

Variant: the paper's own sleep-like periods for the SOM, enrichment and hierarchy claims¶

The change of sleep-like detector between rounds changed several outcomes through the units kept and the retrained clusters. Here the ww and nw SOMs are retrained, and the claims whose outcome moved (fig2f, fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment, extfig3f, extfig5g, fig3a, fig4e, fig4g-gao-category1) are rerun as in their sections, with the sleep-like periods of the paper's own detection files (Zenodo; the probe's file, else another probe's of the session, as in extfig1d). Everything else is as in the main analysis. A variant only: it shows which outcomes depend on the detector.

In [50]:
# Variant: the SOM, enrichment and hierarchy claims rerun from the paper's own sleep-like periods
UZ, RZ = VAR["paper"][1], VAR["paper"][0]
wz = UZ[(UZ.utype == "ww") & (UZ.n_valid >= P.MIN_EPOCHS)].dropna(subset=["log10FR", "B", "M"]).copy()
fz_ww = P.fit_categories(wz, 400, 8)
wz["cat_a"], wz["cat_b"] = fz_ww["cat_a"], fz_ww["cat_b"]
wz["setting5"] = wz.setting.replace({"Opto": "Passive"})
print(f"ww units with >= 12 active epochs: {len(wz)} (main {len(ww_all)}); clusters given the same number by both"
      f" readings: {int((fz_ww['map_a'] == fz_ww['map_b']).sum())} of 8")
print(fz_ww["med"].assign(reading_a=fz_ww["map_a"], reading_b=fz_ww["map_b"]).sort_values("reading_b").round(3).to_string())
VZ = {}

# fig2e and fig2f: block stability

print(f"\nfig2e: stability, mean over transitions {np.mean([P.stability(M)[0] for M in Mz.values()]):.3f} "
      f"(chance {np.mean([P.stability(M)[1] for M in Mz.values()]):.3f}); pooled {P.stability(sum(Mz.values()))[0]:.3f}")
for cat in ["cat_a", "cat_b"]:

    VZ[("fig2f-low-rate-less-stable", "G2 " + cat[-1])] = (p1 and p1x, all(p2))
    print(f"fig2f G2 {cat[-1]}: mean diagonal low {d[[0, 1, 2, 6, 7]].mean():.3f} vs high {d[[3, 4, 5]].mean():.3f}, part 1 {p1}"
          f" (coincidence {p1x}); part 2 for 1, 2, 3, 7, 8: {p2}")

# fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment

cz = selz.region.value_counts()
regz = cz[(cz > 20) & (cz.index != "other")].index
for g1, gcol in [("a", "setting5"), ("b", "setting")]:

                            pops=list(regz) + ["other"], attrs=range(1, 9))
        ra = int((E.loc[six, [1, 2, 3]].sum(1) > 0).sum())
        rb = int(((E.loc[six, [1, 2, 3]] > 0) & (Pv.loc[six, [1, 2, 3]] < 0.05)).any(axis=1).sum())
        VZ[("fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment", f"G1 {g1} G2 {g2}")] = (ra, rb)
        print(f"fig2g G1 {g1} G2 {g2}: subregions of six meeting reading (a) {ra}, (b) {rb}")

# extfig3f-layer-enrichment
cxz = wz[wz.cortical & (wz.layer != "NA")].copy()
cxz["L"] = cxz.layer.str.replace(r"^6[ab]$", "6", regex=True)
for g1, gcol in [("a", "setting5"), ("b", "setting")]:
    for g2 in ["a", "b"]:
        E, Pv, _ = P.escore(cxz.L.values, cxz["cat_" + g2].values, (cxz.region + "|" + cxz[gcol]).values, 1000, seed=12,
                            attrs=range(1, 9))
        sp = (E > 0) & (Pv < 0.05)
        parts = (bool(sp.loc["2/3", [6, 7, 8]].any()), bool(sp.loc["5", [1, 2, 3]].any()), bool(sp.loc["6", [1, 2, 3]].any()))
        VZ[("extfig3f-layer-enrichment", f"G1 {g1} G2 {g2}")] = parts
        print(f"extfig3f G1 {g1} G2 {g2}: L2/3 in 6-8 {parts[0]}, L5 in 1-3 {parts[1]}, L6 in 1-3 {parts[2]}")

# extfig5g-nw-enrichment
nwz = UZ[(UZ.utype == "nw") & (UZ.n_valid >= P.MIN_EPOCHS)].dropna(subset=["log10FR", "B", "M"]).copy()

for ref in "ab":

def vz_outcome(claim, v):
    """the claim's criterion applied to one reading's results"""
    if claim == "fig2f-low-rate-less-stable":
        return "reproduced" if all(v) else ("partially_reproduced" if any(v) else "not_reproduced")
    if claim == "fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment":
        return "reproduced" if min(v) == 6 else ("partially_reproduced" if min(v) >= 4 else "not_reproduced")
    if claim in ("extfig3f-layer-enrichment", "extfig5g-nw-enrichment"):
        return "reproduced" if all(v) else ("partially_reproduced" if any(v) else "not_reproduced")
    if claim == "fig3a-harris-regular-positive":
        return "reproduced" if all(v) else ("partially_reproduced" if v[0] else "not_reproduced")
    if claim == "fig4e-activity-modules":
        if v[0] != v[1]:
            return "readings of ILA-specific disagree"
        return "reproduced" if v[0] and v[2] >= 2 else "not_reproduced"
    return "reproduced" if v[0] else "not_reproduced"

vt = pd.DataFrame([{"claim": c, "reading": rd, "outcome": vz_outcome(c, v)} for (c, rd), v in VZ.items()])
print("\nOutcome of each reading with the paper's own sleep-like periods:")
print(vt.to_string(index=False))
print("\nDistinct outcomes per claim:", vt.groupby("claim").outcome.agg(lambda s: sorted(set(s))).to_dict())

Distinct outcomes per claim: {'extfig3f-layer-enrichment': ['partially_reproduced'], 'extfig5g-nw-enrichment': ['not_reproduced'], 'fig2f-low-rate-less-stable': ['partially_reproduced'], 'fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment': ['partially_reproduced', 'reproduced'], 'fig3a-harris-regular-positive': ['not_reproduced', 'reproduced'], 'fig4e-activity-modules': ['readings of ILA-specific disagree'], 'fig4g-gao-category1': ['not_reproduced']}

Variant result. With the paper's own sleep-like periods 12,324 ww units have at least 12 active epochs (main 12,112), and the retrained SOM's clusters differ. Four of the seven claims keep the outcome they have under the main detector:

  • fig2f-low-rate-less-stable: partially reproduced under both G2 readings (part 1 holds, mean diagonal 0.482 against 0.501 under G2 a and 0.382 against 0.667 under G2 b; part 2 fails for 3 and 8, or 1 and 8). Stability (fig2e) is 56.0% against a chance of 16.6%.
  • extfig3f-layer-enrichment: partially reproduced under every reading (L2/3 and L6 hold, L5 has no significant positive E-score in 1 to 3).
  • fig3a-harris-regular-positive: the outcome still differs under G2 (16 areas). Under G2 b, category 2 has r = 0.56 (p 0.023 to 0.024) with categories 1 and 3 positive (reproduced). Under G2 a, category 2 has r = -0.35 to -0.32 (not reproduced).
  • fig4e-activity-modules: the two readings of "ILA-specific" still disagree. On 24 dataROIs the 2 ILA dataROIs share a module with one PL dataROI under every reading.

Three claims change:

  • fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment: all six subregions qualify under G2 b. Under G2 a, five of six meet reading (a) and all six meet reading (b), which is partially reproduced. G2 would change the outcome (reproduced under the main detector).
  • extfig5g-nw-enrichment: neither part holds under either grouping, which is not reproduced. No PFC subregion and not ORBl is enriched in its category (partially reproduced under the main detector).
  • fig4g-gao-category1: r = 0.04 to 0.27 (p ≥ 0.160) on 29 GaoROIs under every reading, which is not reproduced (blocked by G2 under the main detector).

So the outcomes of fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment, extfig5g-nw-enrichment and fig4g-gao-category1 depend on how sleep-like periods are detected. The main detector is kept, and the paper's periods stay a variant as in extfig1d: they are the paper's output after its visual review ("All sleep-like periods were reviewed visually", Methods), whose rejections the Methods do not describe, and not a detection made from the dataset.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The analyses run on 001260, which holds 74 of the 99 recordings; 000473 is added for the counts, the number of dataROIs and one variant. Units are not filtered by the paper's quality flags, which the files lack (the flags on Zenodo pass 97% of units). Sleep-like periods follow the Methods' detector, applied per session to the pooled cortical units of its probes and skipped where a Poisson population of the same rate would be marked sleep-like 1% of the time or more (a rule of this attempt; the paper describes no skipped session); the paper also reviewed every period visually, and its own detection files mark 19 recordings as not using the detection. The main detector still marks more time (a median 9.9%) than the paper reports (6%). With the paper's own sleep-like periods (a variant), the outcomes of fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment, extfig5g-nw-enrichment and fig4g-gao-category1 would differ, while those of fig2f, extfig3f, fig3a and fig4e stay the same. The SOM, the clustering and the E-scores are re-implemented from the Methods and the code; the SOM grid has 425 nodes, as the code's shape rule gives. An E-score is significant at the 5th or 95th percentile of the shuffles, a 10% two-sided test. Mixed models are fitted with statsmodels and tested by Wald tests, not Kenward-Roger F tests. The retrained clusters cannot be tied to the paper's category numbers, and the two readings of the claims file (G2) disagree for eight claims; projecting the units on the paper's own trained SOM (a variant) gives categories that match the text's descriptions, and under it four of those eight claims hold. Blocks for the stability analysis are taken from the trials table's Block column or cut into 50 onsets. The ZETA onset is computed from zetapy's rate as the first half-peak crossing.

What was found about the dataset. The two dandisets together hold exactly the 29,782 units the paper had before its unit quality control, and the 66 mice; 001260 alone holds 74 recordings, 41 mice and 20,374 units. It carries no label of which units the paper kept, its quality columns are undescribed, and its unit locations, flatmap positions and ww/nw labels need the paper's Zenodo files to be matched to the paper's. The other 25 recordings are in 000473, whose metadata names another paper. Which recordings had their sleep-like detection rejected on review is recorded only in the paper's Zenodo files.
